newsitem.title: CANADA: BASEBALL-BLUE JAYS EXTEND HENTGEN'S CONTRACT THROUGH 2001.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BLUE JAYS EXTEND HENTGEN'S CONTRACT THROUGH 2001.

text.p: The Toronto Blue Jays took steps to keep ace pitcher Pat Hentgen in the fold into the next century on Thursday by agreeing to a contract extension for the American League Cy Young Award winner through the 2001 season.
The agreement guarantees Hentgen's contract through 1999 with options in 2000 and 2001, extending a four-year deal that was signed in April 1995. Financial terms were not disclosed.
The 28-year-old Hentgen recorded more than a quarter of Toronto's 74 wins this past season, posting a 20-10 record.
The right-hander led the majors in innings pitched (265 2/3) and complete games (10), and his 3.22 Earned Run Average ranked second in the league behind teammate Juan Guzman.
